original_question: Let nu_w = S_w(1, ..., 1), the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial S_w. Is it true that nu_w = 2 if and only if the permutation w = a_1 ... a_n has exactly one subsequence a_i a_j a_k with i < j < k and a_i < a_k < a_j, so that w contains exactly one 132 pattern?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 10 of arXiv:2509.25446 (citing [Stan2017, sec. 4 and Conj. 4.1]): the characterization of permutations w for which nu_w = 2 by the existence of exactly one 132-pattern.
correct_elements: Your draft is extremely close to the paper's official formulation. It correctly defines nu_w as the principal specialization S_w(1, ..., 1), correctly identifies this as the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial S_w, and correctly states the target characterization nu_w = 2 in terms of a unique 132-pattern via a unique triple i < j < k with a_i < a_k < a_j.
missing_details: State explicitly that w = a_1 ... a_n is a permutation in S_n, written in one-line notation.
State explicitly that S_w is the Schubert polynomial of the permutation w; for full self-containment one may note that S_w lies in Z[x_1, x_2, ...].
Clarify that S_w(1,1,...) means the principal specialization x_1 = x_2 = ... = 1; this is well-defined because only finitely many variables occur in S_w.
Replace the informal phrase 'contains exactly one 132 pattern' by the precise counting statement that there is exactly one triple (i,j,k) with 1 <= i < j < k <= n and a_i < a_k < a_j.
If one wants to be fully faithful to arXiv:2509.25446 itself, note that the notebook records this as a solved problem rather than an open one, and says it was proved by Weigandt [Cor. 1.3].
refined_question: For a permutation w = a_1 ... a_n in S_n, let S_w in Z[x_1, x_2, ...] be the Schubert polynomial of w, and define nu_w := S_w(1,1,...) (equivalently, the sum of the coefficients of S_w). Is it true that nu_w = 2 if and only if there is exactly one triple 1 <= i < j < k <= n such that a_i < a_k < a_j; that is, w contains exactly one 132-pattern?
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 3, Problem 10, not the broader extremal questions in Problems 11-13. Problem 10 states almost exactly your draft: it defines nu_w as the sum of the coefficients of the Schubert polynomial S_w and asks whether nu_w = 2 exactly when w has a unique 132-pattern. The main improvements needed are only stand-alone clarifications of the domain w in S_n, the one-line notation w = a_1 ... a_n, the meaning of the principal specialization S_w(1,1,...), and the exact counting formulation of 'exactly one 132-pattern.' The notebook also explicitly notes that this statement is recorded there as solved, citing Weigandt's Corollary 1.3.
